newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Serbs must comply with accords to get aid - EU.
newsitem.headline: Serbs must comply with accords to get aid - EU.

text.p: The European Commission insisted on Friday that it would not consider granting aid to the Serb Republic unless it complied with all aspects of peace accords that ended the 43-month Bosnian war.

"As far as the Commission is concerned, any aid should be limited to inter-entity cooperation and those humanitarian projects such as the return of refugees until there is compliance," said Nico Wegter, spokesman for the Commission.

Wegter was speaking to reporters at a news conference on the second day of a World Bank/European Commission meeting of donor states to Bosnia-Herzegovina and following reports that the Commission was prepared to increase aid to the Serb Republic.
The Serb Republic, one of the entities that makes up Bosnia-Herzegovina, has recieved just two percent of over $720 million in international aid since the war ended in late 1995.
On Thursday, both World Bank and European Commission officials said they wanted to "redress the imbalance" and make more funds available to the Serb Republic under the right terms.
The Serb Republic is seen by many governments as unwilling to take its share of blame for the war and has refused to hand over indicted war criminals under terms of peace agreements.

This view has been reinforced by a letter sent by Serb Republic President Biljana Plavsic to new United Nations Secretary-General Kofi Annan vowing not to hand over her predecessor Radovan Karadzic and General Ratko Mladic, both indicted by the International War Crimes Tribunal in The Hague.
The letter, the contents of which were made available to Reuters in New York on Thursday, said handing over Karadzic and Mladic would "threaten the existing peace".
Wegter stressed on Friday that participants at the donor meeting had not agreed on any sum of aid for actual distribution in the Serb Republic.

"We are talking about a framework sum that would be considered if all the right conditions are met," he said. "This is not to say that it has been agreed to give this money ... only inter-entity co-operation is being considered at this moment."

Inter-entity cooperation refers to re-establishing the institutional organisations such as rail links, communications, postal services and power grids between the Serb Republic and the Moslem-Croat federation that make up Bosnia-Herzegovina.

World Bank official Tim Cullen told the news conference the donor meeting had gone very well, and that great progress was being made in Bosnia in establishing Western-style market reforms neccessary for continued international aid.

This week's meeting -- billed by the World Bank as an information meeting -- is a precursor to a full pledging conference to be held in early March at which the World Bank and European Commission are hoping to attract $1.4 billion in aid and investment for Bosnia-Herzegovina for 1997.

Some $1.8 billion has been pledged since the end of the war -- still way short of the estimated $5.1 billion the World Bank believes is neccessary over three years for realistic reconstruction and redevelopment.
